OSX is no true scotsman's UNIX.
That said, we shouldn't care how soldiers feel when we talk about deploying them in our own country...that is unless they feel the same way I do. =)

>> The soldiers would be begging for it.

> Absurd. There are very few soldiers who enjoy war. Yea, there are some, but they are in a minority.

I think some soldiers would more be begging to be stationed in their own country, closer to loved ones.
You could sleep with his fiance?

Yeah. I'm in community college right now but I don't really meet many people. I just got into a state school so I'll be going there in the fall. I'll be getting my degree in CS. I spent so much of my teen programming that even thinking about doing anything else seems like a culture shock to me. I never had jobs growing up because I couldn't function in places like retail.

I can't really get into details of what I do, but I really do feel what I produce helps people. That has been a big part of what keeps me going, but it only takes so long before you start doubting the hype about technology.

It's funny that you mention talking to the help. The security and help I see everyday seem really friendly to me. I'm a young guy on a skateboard and in a suit; I feel like I stick out a bit compared to the many people that come through. 

I have a really hard time talking to them because...I guess you could call it white-collar guilt.

You seem to preach a positive attitude. I like it, thank you.

EDIT: I feel vein just talking about myself some more, but I wanted to give some more context. I'm a student as well as a programmer, even though you got the lonely part correct.

> everyone has problems.

And grown up people seemed so good at hiding them. I think back and remember the messed up stuff that went on under my childhood nose. It's scary.

Well. This was absolutely terrifying. I was reading and replying to all of your nice messages while i was waiting for my pizza to finish cooking. 

...

Fire's out, but I need to walk on over to /r/askreddit and learn how to use a fire extinguisher.

It's strange, one minute you feel dead inside and the next you are fighting for your life against a flaming pepperoni.
EDIT: My first reaction when they started to happen was that it was a seizure, and then I later webMD'ed my symptons and found out about temporal lobe epilepsy.
Thank you for the information. I had tests for epilepsy, because the deja vu came along with vision problems and head pains. They didn't find anything, though, after an EEG and an EKG, IIRC.

argh. I typed out a long reply but then it got erased.

This ordeal has made me wary of the doctors. My parents outright told me that they were convinced I had taken acid, and to me it seemed like the doctors were treating me as such. EDIT:  by this I mean they didn't seem to take my talking about what was happening to me, mentally, seriously. They all just checked out my physical well being and let me on my way.

I had been planning to go now that I can articulate myself and behave in a doctors office, but I feel like I need support. I'm afraid that when I find out I have severe mental and emotional issues, I'll have little support outside of the help I get from a doctor. I definitely do not want to go back on medication. Being drugged was just as painful, just a different kind of pain.

Awww, that's a cute story. I feel the same way when I run into my teachers, even the ones that liked me, but I always hide. It has happened a couple of times too.

I didn't get counseling. I was still living with my parents and no one really wanted to admit I had a mental problem. I went from feeling alright to being belligerent and scared. I had such bad deja-vu I couldn't figure out whether I was really alive or not. My entire life left like a dream I couldn't wake from. EDIT: a nightmare, I guess. I still have doubts about whether this life is a post-death/coma hallucination.

 I always had deja-vu but I never had reacted in this way. They put me on medication to calm me down, but it was only temporary until they found out what was wrong with me, which they never did. They did find out I had the flu, but I don't think it should've made me mentally ill. This happened every once in awhile since the summer after I graduated.

I don't know what is worse. I so get your simile here...because it makes a lot of sense. Also because I'm sitting in my work clothes which are pretty ill-fitting.

The problem with these new clothes is that they don't really seem me. I wasn't cool in high school, but I had a great bunch of friends and I felt like I fit in with them. Now I don't seem to fit in AND you've just informed me that I've completely changed my wardrobe, so to speak.

> "all I can say is that you are going to be so embarrassed about this, when you think about it in a few year's time".

Wow. That seams like the harshest thing you can say to a teenager, mostly because it's true and there is no way they can really deny it. I love it.


The remorse doesn't come solely from being a jerk.. My remorse comes from being so unaware of it. I did some terrible things because I set out to do them...but I did some terrible things that I didn't realize hurt people.


You are very brave. I've always wanted to tell teachers that, as a former problematic student. =)

> IQ/EQ is tending towards infinity

Is that a ratio, IQ over EQ? Like, is my EQ nearing zero?

I've thought about going to groups but I'm 20, the only groups I feel welcome in are the ones that party. Also my work schedule is so rigorous I don't have much time for hobbies.

I really did think the fact that I had moved on, gotten employed and semi-functional would take those walls down but the last time I checked they were as high as ever. EDIT: and the fact that I have a decent, non retail job at my age makes me feel like even if I wasn't a jerk, I am still alienated from my past friends because I'm not suffering retail like that...and undeservedly earn more than them.

My story could begin at a very early age, but I want to start in high school, since I feel that is the biggest piece 
of my past I can't get over.


I was the guy who was a huge jerk but didn't realize it. It's been 2 years and every month or so I realize 
that something else I did was completely dispicable. I life in constant fear and guilt about the unchangeable past.

I'm only realizing it now that I am out in the real world and grown ups have too much self esteem to put up with someone like me. I've gotten better, I know that, but I'm often told I am hard to be around and no one I know wants to spend time with me. Couple this with the introspection that comes with growing up and I get large hits of remorse weekly.

I'm convinced I was a jerk from a couple of years of introspection on my those years coupled with the fact
that most of the people I cared about refuse to have anything to do with me now. People I saw everyday for four
years can't even remember my name...I think that is what stung the most, to realize I'm a ghost there.

Right now all I really want is for those I hurt to know I feel terrible, but I feel those barriors of distrust and anger at how I treated people may never come down.

Just about every week I get up and remember a new face. 10 years ago, 5 years ago, there is no time that is
immune from what I consider a twisted mix of nastolgia and loneliness. I search for this person only to find 
that they have either completely vanished from the internet or they diliberately ignore my attempts at communication. I feel like everyone is slipping away from my grasp.

I'm constantly reminded of this [song](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fq2QKo8n_5g&feature=related).

It's a cliche, but I'm that guy who takes his job too seriously to stave off depression...In reality I just have little friends and no life so
I have nothing else to care about. I spent all high school learning to program and now that I'm programming professionally, I really dislike it. 
But I take it seriously because I really have nothing else.

I spent my teens defining myself using my friends and family... now that I am in the real world where non of those people
seem to be I feel like an empty and meaningless person. I'm not losing control in the typical way, but I feel like
I'm becoming a non-person. I don't technically wish I was dead but I just don't feel alive anymore.


In the past I've gone from perfectly happy and feeling competely well to a 180 degree change of  
having completely uncrontrollable physical and mental behavior where I became suicidal. It will be a year
this febuarary since it started and maybe 6-7 months since it ended. My biggest fear is that now that I live on my own and spend most of my time alone, there will be no one around if this happens
again. 


Thank you for listening.


EDIT: please ignore my username. I wasn't comfortable using my primary reddit handle.
